findings.evidence: Ultrasound skyline view shows bilateral atrophic testes, with measured volumes of 0.32 cc (right) and 0.27 cc (left), far below the normal 12-30 cc range for adult males as stated in the article text.

panels.rationale: Real patient ultrasound image showing bilateral atrophic testes, a classic manifestation of Kallmann syndrome, with clear annotations and supporting evidence from the figure caption and article text; no exclusions apply.
panels.attribution_text: Bothara et al. Diagnosis of Kallmann Syndrome in a Young Adult Male.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.65916. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasound image showing skyline view showing both the atrophic testes.
in_text_mentions: On ultrasonography, normal functioning bilateral kidneys were observed, with a renal calculus noted in the right kidney. In inguino-scrotal ultrasonography, both testes appeared smaller in size, with the right testis measuring approximately 0.32 cc and the left testis measuring approximately 0.27 cc. Normal testis volume typically ranges from 12 to 30 cc. Therefore, in this case, the findings suggested testicular atrophy. Importantly, both testes were observed within the scrotal sac, ruling out cryptorchidism (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Gray-scale pelvic ultrasound from a patient with confirmed Kallmann syndrome, showing a hypoplastic uterus (a classic manifestation of the disease) with poorly visualized ovaries consistent with ovarian hypoplasia. B: Second gray-scale pelvic ultrasound view from the same Kallmann syndrome patient, corroborating the hypoplastic uterus and poorly visualized ovaries seen in panel A. C: Color Doppler pelvic ultrasound from the Kallmann syndrome patient, showing vascular flow in the hypoplastic uterus, consistent with the disease manifestation. D: Second color Doppler pelvic ultrasound view from the same Kallmann syndrome patient, further demonstrating the hypoplastic uterine anatomy and associated vascular pattern.

in_text_mentions: On physical examination, the patient exhibited prepubertal scrotal characteristics, with non‐palpable bilateral testes (Figure 1A,C). Facial hair was absent, including the mustache area; the laryngeal prominence was underdeveloped, and the voice was high‐pitched and soft. Axillary, pubic, and leg hair was sparse. In addition to overt gynecomastia, a firm glandular tissue was palpable beneath the bilateral areolae (Figure 1B). Tanner staging was G1 for genitalia and P2 for pubic hair.
